fact_text: The analyst's oil-shock framework has four checks: how large the supply shock is, whether the government passed prices on to consumers, the market's valuation before the shock, and how far the index corrected.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst holds that when oil rises sharply the government should pass the increase to consumers as quickly and fully as possible, because delay weakens fiscal and physical discipline.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: When fuel prices are raised, consumers cut usage and import volumes fall; when prices are held down, demand stays high and buyers start stockpiling, which inflates the import bill.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In an illustrative example of about 100,000 barrels a day, a 50% international price rise with no local pass-through lifts the monthly fuel import bill from $1 billion to about $1.75 billion.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst argues a fuel subsidy cannot run beyond a few weeks because the subsidy bill exceeds what the state collects in fuel tax, so investors expect prices to be passed on eventually.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: About 20 million barrels a day, roughly 20% of world oil supply, passes through the Strait of Hormuz, so a closure of that strait is a very large supply shock.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Saudi Arabia could export about 5 million barrels a day through alternative routes and the UAE could use other ports, so part of a Hormuz disruption can be offset.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: After offsets from alternative routes and extra output elsewhere, a full Hormuz closure is estimated as a net 10 to 12 million barrels a day shock, close to 10% of supply, similar to 1990.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Countries typically hold about 10 to 30 days of oil supply, so a supply shock reaches industry within roughly 20 to 30 days and tends to push global leaders toward de-escalation.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In the three past oil shocks the index's low formed either before the event or within about 20 to 25 days of it, because markets price expected outcomes early.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst judges an oil-shock episode on one-, two- and three-year index outcomes rather than on the one-to-three-month volatility, which is large and mostly noise.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Across the three past oil shocks the price spike lasted roughly two to six months, and one-to-three-year index results were similar whether the shock faded quickly or lasted longer.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The 1990 oil shock followed Iraq's invasion of Kuwait after OPEC declined to raise prices as Iraq wanted, and Iraq also owed Kuwait a large debt that the attack would address.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The 1990 Gulf shock put about 5 million barrels a day, roughly 7 to 8% of global supply against global demand of about 66 million barrels a day, under threat.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Oil prices rose from roughly $20 to nearly $40 a barrel over the seven months of the 1990 shock and normalised once the coalition liberated Kuwait.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In 1990 Pakistan raised petrol prices by about Rs20 a litre from roughly Rs89, passing the oil shock on to consumers, and later cut them again when oil eased.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan's inflation rose from about 6.4% to 12.66% for the year during the 1990 oil shock, and monthly CPI peaked near 14% in July 1990.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan's current account deficit in FY91 was about $1.25 to 1.5 billion, around 3% of GDP, which the analyst links to the seven-to-eight-month oil shock.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Before the 1990 shock the KSE-100 traded around 7 to 8 times earnings, and its maximum correction during the event was about 16%.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Investing from day 21 after the 1990 invasion, near the oil peak, would have returned about 60% after one year and 111% after two years, with a three-year return reported at about 1,127%.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Iraq produced about 3% of global oil demand before the 2003 US-led war, so its supply was a small share of the global oil shock that year.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In 2003 most of the oil price rise came before the invasion, and prices normalised within about a month after the US declared victory.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst argues the central bank need not hike rates on a supply-driven oil spike that looks temporary; the State Bank did not raise rates in 1990 or 2003 and only hiked in 2022 after devaluation.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: An oil shock becomes a prolonged inflation problem when the rupee devalues and reserves run down, because devaluation keeps inflation high even after oil prices normalise.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The KSE-100 fell about 22% in early 2003 around the oil shock, measured from the level before the event.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In 2003 a 100-point daily KSE-100 move was roughly 4% of the index, so index-point moves should be converted to percentages before comparing volatility across eras.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Investing from day 21 to 25 of the 2003 shock would have returned about 89% after one year, 155% after two years and 321% after three years, according to the analyst's back-test.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Russia exported roughly 5 to 6 million barrels a day of oil and also supplied gas to Europe, so the 2022 Ukraine invasion shock hit both oil and gas together.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In the 2022 shock Pakistan's government delayed passing the oil increase to consumers by about four months, which the analyst links to expected elections making price rises costly.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan's current account deficit rose to about 4% of GDP in 2022, when foreign exchange reserves were around $16 billion.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In the 2022 shock the rupee fell from about 180 to nearly 240 per dollar and inflation passed 25%, after which the State Bank had to raise policy rates.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The KSE-100 corrected about 23% during the 2022 oil shock, starting from a P/E ratio of roughly 8.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Investing 21 days after the 2022 shock would have returned -5.6% after one year, 48% after two years and 165% after three years, as the index moved from about 40,000 to about 100,000.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan passed the oil shock on to consumers in April 2023, and the current account deficit that year fell to about $1.5 billion, roughly 1.5% of GDP.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The current oil shock began in early 2026 with the US-Iran conflict, and Pakistan has joined negotiations to end it, which the analyst credits with improving its geopolitical standing.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: During the 2026 shock Pakistan raised petrol and diesel prices by about Rs55 a litre, and the analyst notes the latest price setting still carried some subsidy.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan's IMF programme has a June 2026 dollar-reserve target, which the analyst expects will push the government toward raising fuel prices to stay on programme.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Governments facing expected elections tend to delay fuel price increases, which lengthens the period over which lagged pass-through weighs on the external account.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: After the 2025 Pakistan-India conflict ended, the index staged a sharp V-shaped recovery, which the analyst linked to Pakistan's improved geopolitical role.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: After the June 2025 Iran-Israel war settled, the market recovered quickly, which the analyst takes as a sign that regional geopolitical shocks have been followed by fast rebounds.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In the 1999 to 2007 boom the KSE-100 rose from about 1,000 to about 14,000, a multi-year rally driven by earnings growth and a rising P/E ratio.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In the 2008 to 2017 boom the KSE-100 rose from about 5,000 to about 55,000, following the same earnings-plus-rerating pattern as the 1999 to 2007 cycle.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A Pakistan boom cycle typically starts with low reserves and single-digit P/E ratios; over seven to eight years earnings roughly double twice and the P/E rises about threefold, giving a 10 to 11 times index gain.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: By the rule of 72, average annual profit growth of about 18% doubles a company's profits in roughly four years, so profits can double twice in about eight years.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Index returns over a boom come from compounding valuation change and earnings growth rather than adding them, so a threefold P/E rise combined with doubled profits multiplies the outcome.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst agrees with observers who say the market cycle since 2023 closely mirrors the 1999 to 2007 cycle, which began after reserves fell and the P/E sank under sanctions.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: When uncertainty fades and local fixed-income returns are low, investors tend to rotate money back into the stock market, which supports valuations.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A market that has already fallen to a low P/E tends to drop less on a negative event, so the valuation before a shock largely determines how deep the correction goes.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)
